paper_assessment.supporting_quote: The present study aimed to investigate the dose-dependent antinociceptive effect of intranasal ketamine (INK) along with behavioral and neurophysiological safety in mice.
paper_assessment.reasoning_summary: The paper is a primary research study investigating the antinociceptive effects and safety of intranasal ketamine in mice, directly supporting claims for a disorder (pain) and related behavioral/physiological outcomes.

claims.outcome_measure: thermal nociceptive threshold / latency to response
claims.supporting_quote: INK administration significantly augmented the thermal nociceptive threshold and alleviated the pain response in the tonic phase of the formalin test. The results showed the dose-independent effectiveness of ketamine for thermal nociceptive responses because there were no significant differences among different INK dose groups.
claims.notes: Dose-independent effect observed for thermal nociceptive responses.

claims.outcome_measure: time spent licking/biting affected paw (tonic phase)
claims.supporting_quote: INK administration significantly augmented the thermal nociceptive threshold and alleviated the pain response in the tonic phase of the formalin test. ... INK (1 mg/kg) markedly inhibited the formalin-induced pain in the tonic phase as indicated by a significant decrease ( P < 0.05) in the time spent licking/biting. Results showed that the formalin-induced nociceptive response was nearly 4 times lesser in ketamine-treated mice.
claims.notes: Effect evaluated at the lowest dose (1 mg/kg).

claims.graph_exclusion_reason: Physiological measure/behavioral side effect, not a primary therapeutic indication.
claims.supporting_quote: However, INK mice showed significantly more stereotypic movement but slower locomotor activities. ... Post hoc analysis showed a significant decrease in locomotor activity of treated groups compared with the control group ( P < 0.001; 5 mg/kg and 1 mg/kg and P < 0.05; 20 mg/kg).
claims.notes: Described as a mild sedative effect.

claims.graph_exclusion_reason: Behavioral side effect, not a primary therapeutic indication.
claims.supporting_quote: However, INK mice showed significantly more stereotypic movement but slower locomotor activities. ... Post hoc multiple comparisons revealed a significant increase in stereotypic movements in treated groups at every dose in comparison to the control group ( P < 0.05).

claims.graph_exclusion_reason: Behavioral safety measure, not a primary therapeutic indication.
claims.supporting_quote: Behavioral safety analysis using the open field exploratory test revealed no significant effect of INK on anxiety-like functions in healthy mice. ... One-way ANOVA showed no significant main effect of treatment ( F 3,24 = 1.261; P = 0.3316) on distance traveled in the center ( Figure 4 A ).
claims.notes: No significant effect on anxiety-like functions.

claims.graph_exclusion_reason: Physiological safety measure, not a primary therapeutic indication.
claims.outcome_measure: heart rate, diastolic blood pressure, systolic blood pressure, mean blood pressure
claims.supporting_quote: No significant changes were reported in heart rate, diastolic blood pressure, or systolic blood pressure at the higher dose equivalent used in the pain model. ... The effect of INK on the systolic pressure, diastolic pressure, mean blood pressure, and heart rate was significantly not different from the control mice ( Figure 5 A-5 D ).
claims.notes: Evaluated at the highest dose (20 mg/kg).

claims.outcome_measure: power spectral density (PSD) in the α band
claims.supporting_quote: The electroencephalography signal power spectrum density analysis revealed no significant changes by INK administration except a lower value in the α range. ... The PSD value in the α band was significantly reduced following INK administration (20 mg/kg) compared with the control (baseline) ( Figure 6 C ).
claims.notes: No significant changes in α power were reported, only PSD value in α band.
